role.en: Patriarch; father of Israel and, in tradition, of many nations

summary.en: The first Hebrew patriarch. Called by God to leave Ur (or Haran) for Canaan under a covenant promise of land and descendants (Genesis 12). Scholars date the patriarchal setting loosely to the Middle Bronze Age (c. 2000-1800 BC) while debating the narratives' historicity and date of composition.

role.en: Matriarch; wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac

summary.en: Wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, buried in the cave of Machpelah at Hebron (Genesis 23).

role.en: Patriarch; son of Abraham, father of Jacob and Esau

summary.en: The promised son of Abraham and Sarah, through whom the covenant line continued; father of Jacob and Esau.

role.en: Patriarch; father of the twelve tribes

summary.en: Son of Isaac, renamed 'Israel' after wrestling at the Jabbok (Genesis 32). His twelve sons are the eponymous ancestors of the tribes of Israel; famine drove his family to Egypt.
Son of Jacob, sold into Egypt and rising to high office, according to Genesis; the narrative frames Israel's settlement in Goshen and sets up the later bondage and Exodus.

role.en: Prophet and lawgiver; leader of the Exodus

summary.en: Leader who, in the biblical account, brought Israel out of Egyptian bondage, mediated the covenant and Law at Sinai, and led the people through the wilderness to the edge of Canaan, dying on Mount Nebo. The Exodus's date and historicity are debated.

role.en: Successor of Moses; led Israel into Canaan

summary.en: Moses' successor who, in the book bearing his name, led Israel across the Jordan near Jericho into Canaan.

role.en: Patriarch of the Flood; builder of the ark

summary.en: The righteous man of Genesis 6-9, warned of the coming Flood and commanded to build an ark of gopher wood, 300 cubits long (Genesis 6:14-15). He preserved his family and the animals through the deluge, landed on the mountains of Ararat, and received the rainbow covenant. The nations of Genesis 10 descend from his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth.

role.en: One of the Seven; the church's first martyr

summary.en: Chosen among the Seven to serve the Jerusalem church, 'full of faith and of the Holy Spirit'. Acts records that he 'did great wonders and signs among the people' (Acts 6:8) before his defence to the Sanhedrin and stoning — witnessed by the young Saul of Tarsus.

role.en: One of the Seven; evangelist of Samaria and the coast

summary.en: One of the Seven (distinct from Philip the apostle). Scattered by the persecution after Stephen's death, he proclaimed Christ in Samaria with exorcisms and healings (Acts 8:6-7), baptized the Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road, and settled at Caesarea, where Paul later lodged with him (Acts 21:8).

role.en: Disciple in Damascus who restored Saul's sight

summary.en: A devout disciple living in Damascus, sent in a vision to the blinded Saul of Tarsus on Straight Street. Laying hands on him, he restored Saul's sight and baptized him (Acts 9:10-19) — the hinge between the persecutor and the apostle.
